items.title: L’OCS, une OTAN asiatique ? | Expliquez-moi…
items.description: En septembre 2026, le sommet annuel de l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghai (OCS) a réuni les dirigeants de ses dix États membres, dont Xi Jinping, Vladimir Poutine et Narendra Modi. Regroupant près de 40 % de la population mondiale, l’organisation est devenue un acteur majeur de la géopolitique eurasiatique. Née dans le contexte de l’après-guerre froide, elle a pour mission première de garantir la sécurité régionale, notamment en luttant contre les « trois fléaux » qu’elle définit comme étant le terrorisme, l’extrémisme et le séparatisme. Ses domaines d'actions se sont cependant largement élargis au cours des dernières années. Souvent présentée comme un pendant oriental de l’OTAN, elle ne constitue pourtant pas une alliance militaire et ne prévoit aucune garantie de défense mutuelle. Ses élargissements successifs, à partir de 2017 avec l’entrée de l’Inde et du Pakistan, ont accru son poids géopolitique, faisant de l’OCS un espace de dialogue et de coopération entre des puissances aux intérêts parfois contradictoires. Entre affirmation de la puissance chinoise, volonté russe de préserver son influence et stratégies de multi-alignement des autres membres, l’OCS illustre une approche des relations internationales fondée sur des partenariats souples plutôt que sur des alliances rigides. L’OCS est-elle une alliance soudée contre l’Occident ? Son élargissement renforce-t-il son poids régional ou accentue-t-il au contraire les divergences qui limitent son efficacité ? Retour en cartes, photos et infographies sur une organisation au cœur des rapports de force en Eurasie. L’article L'OCS, une OTAN asiatique ? | Expliquez-moi… est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Consommer local : Entre prix élevés et faible transformation
items.description: © Internet Créer davantage de valeur en transformant sur place figure parmi les objectifs du Mois du consommer local, célébré en octobre dans l’espace UEMOA. Au Mali, cette campagne coïncide avec le Mois de la solidarité et de la lutte contre l’exclusion. Entre prix, disponibilité et accès aux produits, l’achat local peine encore à devenir un réflexe durable. Les autorités veulent faire de cette campagne un levier de croissance et de souveraineté économique. Le potentiel est important avec le coton, les céréales, les fruits, les légumes et le bétail. Mais la transformation reste limitée. Selon une cartographie du PNUD publiée en 2025, la transformation agroalimentaire ne contribuait qu’à 6,1% du PIB en 2021, laissant une part de la valeur ajoutée hors du pays. La dépendance aux achats extérieurs persiste. En 2025, les importations de produits alimentaires agricoles ont totalisé près de 495 milliards de francs CFA, d’après les bulletins de l’INSTAT. Une facture qui montre la marge disponible pour les producteurs et transformateurs maliens. Manque à gagner En septembre 2026, l’indice des prix à la consommation est resté stable à 109,5 par rapport à août, selon l’INSTAT. Sur trois mois, les prix ont progressé de 1,4% et de 3,4% sur un an. La provenance fait apparaître des évolutions différentes. En septembre, les prix des produits locaux ont reculé de 0,2%, tandis que ceux des produits importés ont augmenté de 0,6%. Sur un an, la hausse atteint 3,9% pour les produits locaux, contre 2,5% pour les produits importés. Le prix n’explique pas tout. Abdel Rahamane Sy, Président de l’Association des Jeunes pour la Valorisation du coton, cite la qualité, la présentation, la sensibilisation et les circuits de distribution parmi les conditions pour rendre les produits maliens accessibles et compétitifs. Hélène N’Diaye, Présidente du Réseau solidaire en agroécologie paysanne citoyenne, récuse l’idée d’un produit local systématiquement plus cher. « Le produit local n’est pas cher, c’est le produit importé qui est faussement bon marché », affirme-t-elle. Son réseau mise sur les marchés de proximité pour réduire les intermédiaires entre producteurs et consommateurs. La transformation, la présentation et une meilleure valorisation des produits doivent aussi permettre d’élargir la clientèle. Le coton résume ce décalage. Selon l’OMC, environ 98% du coton produit dans les pays du C-4+ est exporté sous forme de fibre brute. Le Mali ambitionne d’en transformer localement au moins 10% afin de conserver davantage de valeur ajoutée et d’emplois dans le pays.

items.title: La General Hospital project expected to be completed by end of 2027 – Health Minister
items.description: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says the La General Hospital project, valued at €50 million, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027, with about €15 million paid so far. He gave the timeline during a visit to the project site on Thursday, October 29, 2026, to assess construction progress and identify any challenges that could affect the completion deadline. Mr Akandoh said construction was progressing, adding that the contractor could not cite delayed payments as an excuse for slowing down work, as the government had processed the latest interim payment certificate. “This is quite an impressive development, but they can speed up so that we can beat the deadline,” he said. “The whole project is 50 million euros and we’ve paid about 15 million euros. It includes the hospital equipment, and so now they are at the civil end. When they finish, then they will do the installation and that’s where we also pay as and when they install. The completion date we are looking at is by the end of 2027,” he added. The Minister explained that the project cost covers both construction and hospital equipment, with further payments to be made as equipment is installed. He also stressed the need to prioritise the hospital’s emergency unit to help address the persistent problem of patients being turned away from health facilities because of inadequate emergency beds. Mr Akandoh cited Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, which has a capacity of more than 1,000 beds but approximately 65 emergency beds, as an example of the gap between general bed capacity and emergency care needs. He suggested that emergency beds should account for at least 10 per cent of a hospital’s total bed capacity, noting that the country’s growing population required health facilities to plan adequately for emergency cases. “We learn from experience. Going forward, we correct what we have come to meet,” he said, emphasising the need to improve emergency care provision in new and existing health facilities.

items.title: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports
items.description: The United States has fired a top military planner, US media reported, with some outlets saying the dismissal was due to the officer allegedly leaking classified information. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, US media reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources. CBS and Fox both reported that Sylvia’s dismissal was related to leaks, with the former citing a Pentagon official as saying the general failed three polygraphs about sharing classified information with the media. A spokesperson for the Joint Staff, a top Pentagon body that handles planning and other issues, initially issued a statement that confirmed Sylvia’s departure and wished him well but later withdrew it, saying: “Upon further review, we determined that the statement did not appropriately reflect the full circumstances.” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell then said in a post on X that the Defense Department “has zero tolerance for the intentional, unauthorised disclosure of classified information” and took “necessary personnel action to protect sensitive information.” Parnell did not identify Sylvia by name and said “no further comment will be made regarding the individual or the circumstances of this action”. “This matter, along with others, have been referred to the Justice Department for potential further legal action,” he added. The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Since returning to office early last year, Trump has overseen a purge of top military personnel, including the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, general Charles “CQ” Brown, whom he fired without explanation in February 2025. Renewed Iran strikes? Other senior officers pushed out include the heads of the US Army, Navy and Coast Guard, the general who headed the National Security Agency, the vice chief of staff of the US Air Force, a Navy admiral assigned to Nato, and three top military lawyers. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has insisted the president is simply choosing the leaders he wants, but Democratic lawmakers have raised concerns about the potential politicisation of the traditionally neutral US military. Hegseth said last month that the US had slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 per cent , in a move he said was aimed at “accountability”. He suggested the cuts targeted officers who failed to get on board with his efforts to ensure the military is focused on war-fighting rather than the “woke” policies of previous administrations, describing the reductions as an “accomplishment”. The reported sacking of Sylvia comes as Trump is believed to be weighing fresh strikes against Iran after US midterm elections next Tuesday. “We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump said last week, referring to US-Israeli attacks on Tehran in February that triggered the war . He did not give any indication on timing. Neither the US nor Iran has engaged in major attacks on land-based targets since early September, settling instead into a pattern of strikes on commercial ships. No reason was given for Sylvia’s reported departure. His previous roles included leading the 101st Airborne Division — the US army’s air assault division — and heading a unit in Iraq.

items.title: Burkina : Le ministre de la Sécurité met en garde contre les abus liés à la carte « Laabal »
items.description: Dans un communiqué en date du jeudi 29 octobre 2026, le ministre de la Sécurité Mahamoudou Sana dénonce des pratiques présumées de racket et de corruption impliquant certains agents chargés des contrôles routiers dans l’utilisation de la carte Laabal. Dans son communiqué, le ministre rappelle que cet outil vise à faciliter le paiement des amendes routières et non à exercer une pression sur les usagers. Selon le communiqué, des témoignages de citoyens font état de pratiques contraires à la vocation initiale de la carte Laabal. Certains agents de contrôle routier l’utiliseraient comme un moyen de pression sur des automobilistes et des motocyclistes en infraction, à des fins présumées de racket ou de corruption. Face à ces dérives signalées, le ministre de la Sécurité rappelle que la carte Laabal a été instituée pour éviter la saisie systématique des engins des contrevenants. Elle permet aux usagers de s’acquitter de leurs amendes à une date ultérieure convenue, tout en contribuant à la lutte contre la corruption. Le communiqué précise que cette carte constitue un mécanisme de facilitation pour les usagers en infraction. Elle ne doit donc pas être considérée comme un instrument de contrainte, les travaux d’intérêt commun ne constituant pas sa finalité principale. Dans cette perspective, Mahamadou Sana invite les usagers en infraction à exiger la présentation de la carte Laabal. Cette démarche sera désormais considérée comme un acte citoyen et pourrait constituer une circonstance atténuante, précise le communiqué. Le ministre rappelle également que la route doit demeurer un espace de civisme, fondé sur la courtoisie et le respect mutuel entre les usagers et les agents de sécurité en mission de contrôle. Il souligne que la sécurité et la justice sociale reposent notamment sur la transparence et le respect de la loi. Enfin, Mahamadou Sana a renouvelé ses encouragements aux Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) pour leur professionnalisme, leur intégrité et leur engagement quotidien dans la protection des personnes et des biens sur l’ensemble du territoire national. items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca clôture en grise mine
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a fini sur une note négative jeudi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,74% à 16.801,43 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a baissé de 0,75% à 1.216,8 pts, tandis que le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a reculé de 0,97% à 1.244,31 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a lâché 0,94% à 1.596,35 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Télécommunications » (-2,86%), « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings (-2,85%) et « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (-1,92%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Boissons » (+4,75%), « Agroalimentaire/Production » (+0,35%) ont affiché les uniques performances positives. Les échanges ont dépassé 106,67 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Addoha (15,5 MDH), Attijariwafa bank (15,31 MDH) et Akdital (8,83 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 989,62 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus forts replis ont été accusés par Sonasid (-4,71% à 1.620 DH), HPS (-2,95% à 520,1 DH), Delta Holding (-2,88% à 46,5 DH), Itissalat Al-Maghrib (-2,86% à 85 DH) et T2S Group Holding (-2,86% à 204 DH). Contre-tendance, Société des Boissons du Maroc (+6,21% à 2.018 DH), Maghrebail (+2,27% à 900 DH), Cartier Saada (+2,11% à 19,4 DH), Immorente Invest (+1,12% à 92,98 DH) et Cosumar (+0,57% à 176 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. items.title: Abdoulaye Yaro : « Il faut faire confiance aux jeunes »
items.description: © Internet Expert en management stratégique, en développement organisationnel et en conduite du changement, Abdoulaye Yaro vient de publier son ouvrage « Investir dans la jeunesse ». Il y défend une jeunesse plus engagée et responsabilisée. Dans cet entretien, il revient sur ses motivations, l’importance du leadership et la responsabilité des décideurs. Propos recueillis par Mohamed Kenouvi Pourquoi avoir consacré un livre à l’investissement dans la jeunesse ? La jeunesse constitue l’essentiel de notre population. Plus de 74% des Maliens ont moins de 30 ans et l’âge moyen est de 21 ans et demi. Si nous voulons progresser, nous devons renforcer nos efforts en direction des jeunes. Ce livre s’appuie sur près de vingt ans d’engagement, d’abord comme leader d’organisations de jeunes, puis comme porteur d’initiatives destinées à valoriser leur place dans la société. L’objectif est de les encourager à construire le présent et à assumer des responsabilités pour l’avenir. Vous insistez sur le leadership. Comment les jeunes peuvent-ils le développer ? Tout commence dans la famille, que je considère comme la première école du leadership. C’est là que l’on découvre l’autorité. Ensuite, les jeunes doivent développer leurs capacités sur le terrain, au sein des organisations de jeunesse et des associations, ainsi qu’à travers leurs initiatives communautaires. Ces expériences renforcent leur sens des responsabilités et leur permettent de participer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Votre livre, édité par Bandama Éditions, a été préfacé par l’ancien Premier ministre Moussa Mara. Comment s’est faite cette collaboration ? Les questions relatives à la jeunesse intéressent énormément Moussa Mara. Il a donc accepté de préfacer ce livre et de donner son avis sur cette problématique. Sa contribution nourrit la réflexion que nous souhaitons susciter autour de l’investissement dans la jeunesse et de son rôle dans le développement du Mali. Ce livre constitue un plaidoyer pour la jeunesse. Quel message adressez-vous aux jeunes et aux décideurs ? Je m’adresse d’abord aux jeunes, car ils sont les premiers acteurs de leur développement. Je les invite à accepter de prendre des responsabilités et à défendre les valeurs évoquées dans l’ouvrage. Mais j’interpelle également les décideurs. Il ne s’agit pas uniquement des autorités publiques, mais de tous ceux qui exercent des responsabilités : directeurs d’école, chefs de famille, chefs d’entreprise, entre autres. Je leur demande de faire confiance aux jeunes et de leur donner la possibilité d’assumer des responsabilités. C’est ainsi qu’ils pourront démontrer leurs capacités. Je reste convaincu qu’ils sont capables de relever les défis auxquels nous sommes confrontés.

items.title: MTN Bright Scholarship supports 500 students and teachers for 2026/2027 academic year
items.description: MTN Ghana has awarded scholarships to 500 students and teachers for the 2026/2027 academic year under its flagship MTN Bright Scholarship initiative, aimed at supporting brilliant but financially needy individuals to pursue their educational ambitions. The scholarship, spearheaded by the MTN Ghana Foundation, provides financial assistance to beneficiaries through tuition fees, hostel accommodation, stipends and laptops to support their academic work and research. The award ceremony brought together beneficiaries, guardians, academics and MTN officials to celebrate the opportunities created through the initiative. Senior Manager of MTN Scholarship, Robert Kuzoe, said the current cohort forms part of a three-year programme designed to support 500 beneficiaries annually, comprising 300 students and 200 teachers, with a focus on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) and related disciplines. “This is the second cohort that we are doing. And with each cohort, we give scholarships to 500 needy but brilliant students. Also, we’ve not left out teachers; we do the same for teachers. So, with the 500, we have 300 students and then 200 teachers who are also in the STEM areas. ”Now, the scholarship comes with tuition, hostel fees, a stipend, and also a laptop just for the students to be comfortable and be able to study hard and do their own research in school,” he asserted. Mr Kuzoe urged beneficiaries to make the most of the opportunity and use their education to contribute meaningfully to society. He said the scholarship is open to eligible applicants from both public and private universities, provided they fall within the designated STEM and STEAM categories. He added that the programme also seeks to encourage women to pursue science-related fields. “Applications are open to all universities, provided you find yourself within the STEM and STEAM categories. Women are also encouraged to find their way into the sciences. So it’s open to all, but it’s very competitive because you have to apply, you’ll be interviewed, you go to a shortlisting process,” he noted. According to Mr Kuzoe, more than 5,000 applications were received nationwide, with the number reduced to 1,200 during shortlisting before the final 500 beneficiaries were selected, highlighting the competitive nature of the programme. He explained that the annual allocation of 500 scholarships is intended to run for three years, after which MTN will consider the next steps for the initiative. For some beneficiaries, the scholarship represents a significant relief from the financial challenges that have threatened their education. A Level 400 student at the University for Development Studies (UDS), Gilbert Abongo, from the Bongo District in the Upper East Region, said he struggled to continue his education after completing senior high school more than a decade ago. Mr Abongo, who had long hoped to use education to change the circumstances of people in his hometown, said financial constraints forced him to combine his university studies with work at a kebab-selling business to support himself. “I was facing financial difficulties, and it wasn’t easy for me. I completed SHS ten years ago, but I never gave up. I had the opportunity to go to school. Things were not easy for me, so I spoke to a man who sells kebab at UDS to work with him, and he agreed. I was combining school with the job. When I was struggling, one of the beneficiaries of the MTN Bright Scholarship,” he said. The initiative forms part of the MTN Ghana Foundation’s broader efforts to expand access to education and develop skills in fields considered important for Ghana’s development, while easing the financial burden on students, teachers and their families. Meanwhile, Esther Quaye, a guardian whose sister benefited from the scholarship, described the award as a major relief for their family, which has been facing financial hardship. “I was very, very excited because our family is going through some hot shifts, and so it was a very huge relief that she won the award, especially with all the things that come with their accommodation, the tuition, and then the stipends and, most importantly, the laptop that they are getting; it’s really refreshing. It has brought some kind of relief to the family. So yes, we are very much happy about it,” she said.

items.title: NLC faults Tinubu’s fresh external loan request
items.description: By Olayinka Ajayi The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to obtain fresh external loans of $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion, questioning the justification for continued borrowing. NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, said the basis for the proposed loans was unclear, particularly in view of the Federal Government’s claims of increased revenue following the removal of petrol subsidy. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Ajaero challenged the government to explain why it continued to seek loans from international financial institutions despite the reported increase in revenue. “If you come out to tell us that the subsidy is gone, that you are making more money and then you are giving more money to states, what is the justification for continually borrowing from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and other agencies when there is enough money?” he asked. The labour leader argued that continued borrowing was worsening the country’s debt burden, adding that international financial institutions lending to Nigeria were not necessarily acting in the country’s best interests. He also cited rising crude oil prices, which he attributed to tensions in the Middle East, as another reason the government should reconsider its borrowing plans. “If the 2026 budget was prepared with crude oil price benchmarked at $70 per barrel and now sells above $100 per barrel due to the US-Iran crisis, should this country still be collecting loans?” Ajaero asked. He maintained that increased oil earnings and revenue accruing to oil-producing states should prompt the government to explain why additional external borrowing remained necessary. Ajaero, however, clarified that the NLC had no authority to approve or reject government loans, noting that such decisions rested with the relevant government institutions. He urged Nigerians and relevant agencies to demand greater accountability from the Federal Government over its borrowing plans. The NLC president also pointed to the role of the National Assembly, saying lawmakers could stop the proposed borrowing by rejecting the request for approval. He called for greater scrutiny of the loans and their justification, given the implications of mounting public debt for the country’s economy. The post NLC faults Tinubu’s fresh external loan request appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rana Sanaullah says Imran's jailed sister Noreen 'fine' after being provided medical treatment
items.description: Adviser to the prime minister on political affairs, Rana Sanaullah, on Thursday informed the Senate that Noreen Niazi, the sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, was fine after being provided medical treatment in Lahore. Imran’s three sisters — Noreen, Aleema Khan, and Uzma Khan — have been in detention since Sept 21 under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO) on the Lahore deputy commissioner’s (DC) orders. On Wednesday, Noreen’s lawyer said that she was moved from Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) due to high blood pressure. Her lawyer claimed that no family member had been informed about her deteriorating health condition. Speaking on the floor of the Senate on Thursday, Sanaullah responded to the query by PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Ali Zafar, who sought information regarding Noreen’s health and her being taken to the hospital. The PML-N senator said Noreen was “immediately provided with medical facilities”. “As per the information available, she is fine and all her medical tests are normal,” he said. On concerns about Noreen’s family allegedly not being allowed to meet her, the prime minister’s adviser said details would also be sought on the matter. He assured the PTI that if this was true, it would be addressed depending on the circumstances at the hospital. During his address, PTI Senator Mashal Yousafzai continued to interrupt Sanaullah, questioning the need for Noreen’s detention. The PML-N senator replied: “She is in jail because she wanted to spread turmoil in the country. She wanted to attack Islamabad by launching a long march and inciting the people.” Addressing Zafar, Sanaullah said that as the PTI founder was in jail under judicial custody, any relief regarding his health and meeting should be sought from the courts. Imran’s sisters are currently serving the second term of a 30-day detention under the MPO, which was extended on Oct 7. The detention came amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party had called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. ‘Must never allow our humanity to fail’ In his remarks on the Senate floor, Zafar contended that Noreen had been detained despite not having committed any crime. While Noreen’s lawyer had said she had faced high blood pressure, Zafar said she suffered a heart attack and claimed that her family was not being allowed to meet her. Quoting Shakespeare’s phrase “milk of human kindness”, Senator Zafar said if even a little human kindness remained, the government must immediately stop grave human rights violations. “If there is even a minimum of human kindness left in you, release her. At least allow her family to meet her and ensure proper medical care,” he said while speaking on a point of order. He also condemned the detention of Imran’s nephews, asking why family members should suffer for their relationship with a political leader. He alleged Imran had been kept in solitary confinement for a year and was being subjected to torture, claiming that the PTI founder’s wife Bushra Bibi was also facing inhumane treatment. He demanded an immediate end to their mistreatment, which the government denies , saying both are being provided with the facilities they are entitled to. Zafar claimed that the government believes the Constitution can be broken and suspended, as witnessed in the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has rendered the elected provincial government non-functional. “There is one thing that cannot be broken, suspended or compromised: the fundamental human rights of the people of Pakistan,” he asserted. Senator Zafar stressed that even if governor’s rule was claimed to be justified, it could never be a licence to violate fundamental rights, detain the chief minister, speaker and elected representatives, or keep their whereabouts undisclosed. He warned that violating the sanctity of home and family honour, which hold deepest importance in Pashtun society, would provoke strong resentment among people of KP. He also referred to reports of attacks on homes of MNAs and alleged violence against their wives and sisters, calling for impartial investigation. “These are not merely political issues. These are matters of human rights, human dignity, family honour and rule of law. Human rights stand above politics,” he said. Concluding, he said: “The Constitution may be violated by those who wield power, democratic mandates may be undermined, and institutions may fail in their duty. But we must never allow our humanity to fail.” PTI condemns Noreen’s hospital transfer ‘sans informing family’ Meanwhile, in a statement, the PTI condemned the transfer of 70-year-old Noreen to the PIC without informing her family, expressing grave concern over her health and the treatment of “political prisoners”. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram criticised the authorities for not informing Noreen’s family after she felt unwell while in custody at the Kot Lakhpat jail. He described the handling of her medical emergency as “callous and inhumane”, arguing that denying family members timely information about the condition of an elderly heart patient raised serious questions about prisoners’ rights, legal safeguards and basic human dignity. “Noreen Niazi’s transfer to the PIC without prior notification to her family is alarming,” Akram said, demanding an immediate explanation from the Punjab government and the relevant authorities. He demanded that Noreen receive the best possible medical treatment under the supervision of senior cardiologists without any delay, that her necessary diagnostic tests be conducted, and that her family be allowed access in accordance with applicable law. “The authorities must provide her family with complete, credible and timely information about her condition,” the PTI leader further stressed. Warning the government against disregarding fundamental rights in the alleged pursuit of political objectives, he said the PTI would not compromise on the protection of human life, health or constitutional freedoms under any circumstances. Additional input by Ikram Junaidi

items.title: NIA arrests six staff, dismisses seven over alleged Ghana Card extortion
items.description: The National Identification Authority (NIA) has announced the arrest of six staff members and the termination of the appointments of seven others over alleged extortion during the free Ghana Card registration exercise at Galaka in the Upper East Region. The disciplinary action follows complaints that some registration officials demanded money from parents before registering their children during the recently concluded exercise for children aged six to 14. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, the Authority disclosed that the six staff members, who were identified by affected parents, had been arrested by the Bawku West District Police and were assisting with investigations. The NIA further revealed that an extensive internal review had resulted in the dismissal of seven other members of the registration team who were found to have known about the alleged misconduct but failed to report it. The Authority stressed that the Ghana Card registration exercise must be conducted strictly in accordance with approved procedures, emphasising that no official is permitted to demand unauthorised payments from applicants or their parents. It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining transparency and accountability in its operations, warning that misconduct would attract appropriate disciplinary sanctions. The NIA also assured the public that it would continue to take the necessary measures to safeguard the integrity of its registration processes and ensure that applicants receive fair and professional services. It consequently encouraged members of the public to report suspected misconduct by registration officials through its official communication channels. The statement was signed by Williams Ampomah Emmanuel Darlas, Head of the Corporate Affairs Directorate of the NIA.

items.title: INEC moves to tackle electoral risks in Abia
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has stepped up preparations for the 2027 general elections, with efforts to identify and address potential threats to peaceful and credible polls in Abia State. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, Prof. Sylvia Agu, disclosed this on Thursday in Umuahia at a stakeholder sensitisation workshop on Electoral Risk Management (ERM). Agu said early identification of electoral threats, effective coordination and collaboration among stakeholders were critical to preventing disruptions and strengthening public confidence in the electoral process. “Successful elections require deliberate preparation, effective coordination and the collective commitment of all institutions and individuals involved in the electoral process,” she said. She urged stakeholders, particularly security agencies, to sustain their cooperation with INEC to ensure peaceful elections and strengthen democracy. The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, also reaffirmed the police commitment to credible elections. Represented by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, DCP Ifeanyi Uzor, Afolabi said the police would protect election materials, provide security for National Youth Service Corps members and ensure a safe environment for voters. “The 2027 election will not be an exception. We have a renewed commitment from the Inspector-General of Police to ensure credible elections in 2027. That duty we must perform without fear or prejudice,” he said. Also speaking, the INEC Administrative Secretary in Abia, Chief Ama Agwu, said the ERM framework would help identify, assess and manage security threats, political tensions, environmental challenges and operational difficulties capable of disrupting elections. Agwu urged electoral officers to ensure that information gathered was accurate, verified and reflective of conditions on the ground to facilitate timely interventions. Earlier, the Head of the Department of Planning and Monitoring, Mr Ogbuisi Robinson, said the workshop was designed to identify electoral risks specific to Abia, strengthen early-warning and response mechanisms, and promote evidence-based planning. He said the exercise would also involve collaboration with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). INEC officials, including Electoral Officers from all 17 local government areas in Abia, representatives of security agencies and other stakeholders attended the workshop. items.title: 3 dead in rock spire collapse at tourist site in Turkiye's Cappadocia
items.description: A landslide triggered by heavy rainfall caused a rock spire to collapse in Turkiye’s Unesco World Heritage-listed Cappadocia region on Thursday, bringing the death toll to three, officials said. Turkiye’s Cappadocia region, a magnet for tourists from around the world, is home to cone-shaped rock formations known as “fairy chimneys”, created by ancient volcanic activity. “According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on X. Rescue teams pulled another body from the rubble, bringing the death toll to three, Nevsehir Governor Huseyin Kok said. The nationalities of the dead were not immediately known. “Search and rescue teams are continuing intensive, coordinated operations to locate any other victims who may be trapped under the debris,” the minister said. Television footage showed heavy machinery digging through the rubble as rescue teams gathered at the site in an effort to recover people. Excavators and rescue workers worked into the night at the site, using powerful floodlights as the search operation continued. This handout photograph taken and released on October 29, 2026 by Turkish news agency DHA (Demiroren News Agency) shows rescue teams searching for victims at the site of a rock formation that collapsed due to a landslide triggered by heavy rains in Cappadocia district of Nevsehir. — AFP The incident occurred at 3:15pm local time (5:15pm PKT) when a landslide triggered a rockfall in the town of Goreme near the open-air museum, local governor Kok said. The area was closed to the public following the collapse, according to reports. Eyewitnesses described hearing a loud noise as the rock spire near a car park collapsed, sending up a huge cloud of dust. Restoration Turkiye’s culture and tourism ministry has launched restoration work in the region to help preserve the fragile rock formations from climate-related damage, natural erosion and human activity. In 2024, another rockfall was reported in Cappadocia, although no deaths or injuries were recorded. A Unesco heritage site since 1985, Goreme national park and the rock sites of Cappadocia are “a landscape of harmony combining human interaction and settlement with dramatic natural landforms,” according to the UN agency. Some of the cones and pillars have experienced earthquake damage, but this is seen as a naturally occurring phenomenon. “Overuse by tourists and some vandalism have been reported and some incompatible structures have been introduced,” it said on its website. The Cappadocia region is also home to rock-carved underground cities and early Christian churches. In 2025, some 4.5 million domestic and foreign tourists visited the region, according to tourism ministry figures. Hot-air ballooning in Cappadocia is a thriving industry that sees dozens of balloons take to the skies on clear mornings. But concerns have been raised about safety following a series of accidents.

items.title: MSF calls for stronger security measures to protect its work in Central Darfur
items.description: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has called on authorities in Central Darfur to remove commercial sites surrounding Zalingei Teaching Hospital and Starlink networks from inside the facility, as it seeks better protection for its medical teams and safer movement across the state. The requests were made during a meeting between Major General Mohamed Adam El Banjous, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) commander in Central Darfur, and a team from the Spanish section of MSF. The meeting discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and coordination to facilitate the organisation’s work and secure the movements of its medical teams in the state. The state’s civil administration media office said MSF had confirmed that it would continue supporting Zalingei Teaching Hospital and other health centres, providing emergency care, paediatric services, and responses to diseases and epidemics, including measles. MSF also called for the activation of security agreements signed with the state’s security committee to address challenges affecting its medical operations. The organisation said it provides services in several parts of Central Darfur, including Zalingei, Wadi Salih, Mukjar, and northern Jebel Marra. It stressed the importance of protecting its teams and enabling them to travel safely between these areas. El Banjous praised MSF’s efforts to provide medical services in the state and said the RSF was responsible for protecting and securing humanitarian and health-related activities and facilities. He urged the organisation to strengthen coordination with the RSF leadership in the state to ensure the safety of its staff and enable them to carry out their duties. items.title: Duo Wally Seck-Baaba Maal: Marva Music revisite le répertoire de Thione Seck
items.description: Deux voix. Deux signatures. Deux personnalités. En route vers le festival « Les Blues du fleuve » (4-6 décembre 2026 à Podor et Ndioum), Baaba Maal et Wally Seck se retrouvent dans le cadre d’un projet musical piloté par Marva Group. La nouvelle boîte de production Marva Music revisite les tubes qui ont marqué la discographie de Thione Seck en réunissant Baaba Maal et Wally Seck. Préférant garder la surprise pour les mélomanes, le président directeur général de Marva Group, Mamadou Diop, n’a pas dévoilé les titres qui seront remis au goût du jour. M. Diop a renouvelé l’engagement de Marva Group à apporter son savoir-faire et son dispositif exceptionnel pour donner une nouvelle dimension au festival « Les Blues du fleuve » dont l’avant-première est prévue le 27 novembre au Théâtre Daniel Sorano de Dakar. De la réussite du Grand Bal de Youssou Ndour à d’autres grands rendez-vous, Marva Group a toujours été au cœur des événements d’envergure au travers de son dispositif technique. Dénommé le roi du yéla, Baaba Maal est un artiste légendaire. Inspiré de la culture peule, avec son groupe « Le Daandé Leñol » (La voix du peuple), il a conquis le showbiz mondial avec ses prestations scéniques et des albums d’une dimension musicale rare. L’artiste est également un grand défenseur des causes sociales. Il est à l’origine de plusieurs projets sociaux, culturels et économiques au Sénégal et en Afrique. Le Festival « Les Blues du fleuve », qui a lieu tous les ans aux abords du fleuve Sénégal, en est une belle illustration. Pour le roi du yéla, « Les Blues du Fleuve » est plus qu’un festival : c’est un lieu de convergence pour les peuples riverains du fleuve Sénégal, un espace de partage, de musique et d’identité. Sur ce registre, l’héritier de Thione apportera une touche de fraîcheur en chantant avec Baaba Maal. E. Massiga FAYE

items.title: NPP demands Sports Minister’s resignation over visa controversy
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called for the resignation of the Minister for Youth and Sports over allegations of irregularities in arrangements for Ghanaian personnel linked to activities surrounding the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The party’s National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, made the demand at a press conference on Thursday, October 29, 2026, linking the controversy to the resignation of the National Sports Authority (NSA) Chief Executive Officer, Yaw Ampofo Ankrah. Mr Yakubu argued that the circumstances surrounding Mr Ampofo Ankrah’s departure warranted similar action by the minister. “To the Ministry of Youth and Sports, the minister must also resign. The visa scandal, the facilitation that led to the resignation of Mr Ampofo, the Chief Executive Officer for the National Sports Authority, confirmed that there were indeed scandals, and we require the minister to also resign,” he said. The controversy centres on allegations of payments of up to US$14,000, questions about the identities of personnel submitted for visa processing and the use of job titles that allegedly did not exist. The Minority in Parliament has also raised concerns about lists of personnel submitted to foreign diplomatic missions in connection with Ghana’s participation in activities surrounding the 2026 FIFA World Cup. According to the Minority, only two of the 50 names submitted by the Ghana Tourism Authority to the United States Embassy as media personnel were verified as professional media practitioners. It further alleged that only 15 of the 102 names submitted by the NSA to the Canadian Embassy were verified as actual employees of the authority. These claims have been cited in the wider debate over the selection and documentation of personnel for World Cup-related activities. President John Dramani Mahama asked Mr Ampofo Ankrah to step aside amid the controversy. Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong was subsequently appointed acting Director-General of the NSA. The NPP is now extending its demand for accountability to the minister responsible for the sector. The minister had not publicly responded to the party’s call for his resignation at the time of the press conference. The NPP’s demand adds to the political pressure on the government to address the allegations surrounding the visa arrangements. The key issues include the verification of personnel submitted for visa processing, the basis for any payments reportedly made and whether any public officials breached applicable procedures.

items.title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. A formal trial commenced after both lawyers pleaded not guilty. Both were on bail in this case prior to the verdict. Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict in the case at Adiala jail on Thursday, where the trial was conducted. The sentence was handed down under three separate legal provisions. According to the judgment, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the two were sentenced to ten years along with a fine of Rs100,000 each under Section 7 (h) of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, as defined under Section 6 (2) (m) — serious coercion or intimidation of a public servant in order to force him to discharge or to refrain from discharging his lawful duties. The court further handed down a one-year sentence and fined Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Imaan and Hadi were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the PPC. All the sentences will run concurrently, the judgment stated. Judge Sipra held that the two were “jointly responsible for the offence committed under joint object and common intention”. He stated that the objective of the accused was to “compromise the security arrangements through pressuring security officials”. While the court acknowledged that the right of movement was a constitutional right, it held that the “same right is subject to observance of the law of the land, and nobody is allowed to attack/assault” law enforcement agencies. The judgment, citing the attack on the Sri Lankan cricket team in Lahore in 2009, stated that the assault on police personnel and the attempt to “put the security of an international team visiting Pakistan at risk clearly shows the intentions and objective of the accused to create sense of terror”. The court maintained that the two were well-educated persons “having the full knowledge of delicacy of the matter, but they assaulted upon the police officials deputed [there] for ensuring [..] security”. Meanwhile, on charges under Section 506 ii (punishment for criminal intimidation), 120-B (punishment of criminal conspiracy), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), and 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object) of the PPC, both Imaan and Hadi were acquitted. The court had appointed a state counsel for the defence in the case. State counsel Atif Mehmood conducted the cross-examination of the witnesses during the trial, while the prosecution presented a total of seven witnesses. On Oct 27, both accused recorded their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), while final arguments by the state counsel also concluded during the proceedings. On Monday, the couple approached the SC to challenge the IHC’s Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case. The IHC had heard their appeals last week against an Oct 10 ATC order dismissing petitions challenging the framing of charges and the inclusion of terrorism-related provisions. The high court issued notices and said it would decide how to proceed after receiving responses from the parties. ‘Prisoners of conscience’ In their statements recorded under Section 342 of the CrPC, Imaan and Hadi had denied the charges and alleged that they were being targeted for their human rights work and provision of pro bono legal assistance and services to the marginalised and oppressed communities. “The evidence produced during this trial is not against us, but in fact a charge sheet against (prosecution witnesses)/police officials and the state,” Imaan and Hadi said in their separate similar recorded statements available with Dawn. “I am a prisoner of conscience who has been at the receiving end of state persecution,” the statements read. Imaan pointed out that the entire jail trial had been challenged by the couple in the IHC as well as the SC. Further, the trial was conducted with Imaan and her husband being presented in a cage, preventing effective communication with their counsel or the court, she said. “From day one, our constitutional rights to fair trial, due process and basic human dignity have been infringed,” she stated. She also noted that the couple had been incarcerated for over nine months and handed 17-year sentences a day after their arrest on January 23. “We are being made an example to further cement the chilling effect against those who stand (or want to stand) against tyranny, oppression and injustice,” Imaan stated. The lawyer further highlighted that the two had spent the third year of their marriage in jail and thus “suffered painful separation from one another” very early on. “We have not done so for any personal gain; in fact, we have endured only hardship for our work (and) activism,” she said. “But we surrender ourselves before the ultimate court where we all must return one day, where all will be held accountable for what they have done.” Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

items.title: Algérie : Un tournant militaire au Niger
items.description: © Internet L’Algérie s’apprête à envoyer certaines unités de son armée au Niger, une première depuis plus d’un demi-siècle. Présentée par Alger comme une mission de protection d’intérêts énergétiques et économiques communs, la décision marque un tournant dans la manière dont le pays envisage sa sécurité hors de ses frontières. Le Président Abdelmadjid Tebboune a confirmé le 26 octobre l’envoi d’unités de l’Armée nationale populaire à Madama, dans l’extrême nord du Niger, près de la frontière libyenne. Le Parlement algérien avait approuvé la veille cette projection militaire, demandée par Niamey. Les effectifs, la durée et le calendrier précis du déploiement n’ont pas été rendus publics. Le choix de Madama ajoute au symbole. La France y avait installé en 2014 une base avancée de l’Opération Barkhane, destinée notamment à surveiller les routes reliant le sud libyen au Sahel. Cette position, mise en sommeil en 2019, permettait de contrôler des flux d’hommes, d’armes et de trafics dans une zone stratégique entre Libye, Niger, Mali et Algérie. Située à une centaine de kilomètres de la Libye, elle donne accès aux routes qui descendent du Fezzan vers Agadez et les espaces sahéliens plus au sud. Doctrine Pendant des décennies, Alger a privilégié la défense de son territoire et s’est montrée réticente aux interventions militaires étrangères dans son voisinage sahélien. Sa Constitution, révisée en 2020, autorise toutefois l’envoi de troupes hors du pays après approbation des deux tiers de chaque Chambre. Le dispositif juridique existait. Madama lui donne une traduction militaire majeure. Le rapprochement avec Niamey repose aussi sur des intérêts économiques précis. Sonatrach poursuit des activités d’exploration dans le bloc de Kafra, tandis que le projet de gazoduc transsaharien doit relier le Nigeria à l’Algérie en passant par le Niger. La sécurisation du nord nigérien touche ainsi directement des investissements et des corridors que l’Algérie considère comme stratégiques. La décision intervient après une période de relations tendues avec Niamey, notamment après le coup d’État de 2023 et les différends régionaux liés à la sécurité sahélienne. Les échanges politiques et militaires ont depuis repris, jusqu’à cette nouvelle étape. Le contraste est saisissant. Une ancienne base avancée française, symbole d’une présence militaire occidentale souvent regardée avec méfiance par Alger, pourrait servir aujourd’hui au premier déploiement extérieur algérien depuis 1973. La doctrine de retenue n’a pas disparu, mais elle s’accompagne désormais d’une capacité assumée à se projeter chez un voisin lorsque des intérêts sécuritaires, économiques et énergétiques sont directement concernés.

items.title: NPP announces November 3 ‘Y3gye y3 Sika’ protest over South Africa evacuation and passport controversies
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has announced a nationwide demonstration on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, to demand the dismissal of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and investigations into controversies surrounding an evacuation exercise and the issuance of passports. The protest, dubbed “Y3gye y3 sika” , is intended to press the government for greater accountability over public expenditure on the evacuation and the issuance of diplomatic and service passports. Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, October 29, the NPP’s National Youth Organiser, Abanga Fuseini Yakubu, called on party supporters and other Ghanaians to participate in the demonstration. “The public money belongs to the people, so do the official documents of the Republic. The ministers hold them in trust, and when the trust is abused, it is the people who must rise and demand accountability,” he said. The NPP has accused the minister of wrongdoing in connection with the matters, but the allegations require investigation and should not be treated as established findings. Mr Yakubu said demonstrators would assemble at 6:00 a.m. at Villaggio, near the Tetteh Quarshie Interchange and opposite Accra Mall. The planned route will include a stop at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs before ending at Jubilee House, the seat of government. He urged the party’s youth organisers, constituency and polling station executives, women’s groups and other supporters to mobilise for the protest. Mr Yakubu also called for a peaceful demonstration, saying participants should remain disciplined and act within the law. “Our strength is in our numbers and our discipline, never in disorder,” he said. He added that the party would continue to demand answers until the issues were addressed. The party has outlined several demands, including the immediate dismissal of Mr Ablakwa as Foreign Affairs Minister. It is also calling for investigations by the Attorney-General and the Office of the Special Prosecutor, with the prosecution of the minister and any other officials found culpable. On the evacuation exercise, the NPP wants the government to publish the original invoices, contracts and proof of payment for all charter flights. It is further demanding the release of the full passenger manifest and beneficiary list to verify the reported evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians, alongside an independent audit of the total expenditure. On passports, the party wants the publication of details of all diplomatic and service passports issued since January 2025, including the qualifying office or status of each recipient and the approving authority. It is also calling for the cancellation of any passports found to have been issued improperly. The planned demonstration marks a further escalation in the NPP’s criticism of Mr Ablakwa over the evacuation expenditure and passport-related controversies. The party has also called for the resignation of the Minister for Youth and Sports over a separate visa controversy that preceded the resignation of the National Sports Authority’s chief executive. The demonstration is scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

items.title: Sécurité sanitaire des aliments : Le LaNSA se fait connaître des acteurs régionaux à Sokodé
items.description: Sokodé, 29 oct. (ATOP) – Le Laboratoire national de sécurité sanitaire et phytosanitaire des aliments (LaNSA) a été présenté aux acteurs régionaux réunis en atelier les 27 et 28 octobre à Sokodé. Les travaux ont été couplés d’une sensibilisation sur la sécurité sanitaire et phytosanitaire des aliments. L’atelier a été organisé par le LaNSA dans le cadre de sa tournée nationale visant à se faire connaître et à rapprocher ses services des acteurs des chaînes de valeurs agricoles. L’objectif est de promouvoir le respect des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et de fabrication tout en contribuant au renforcement de la compétitivité des produits togolais pour booster l’économie des territoires. Les participants ont suivi une présentation sur le LaNSA, sa mission, ses attributions, ses services et son rôle dans le contrôle des aliments. Les enjeux de la sécurité alimentaire et phytosanitaire des aliments pour la santé des consommateurs et la compétitivité des produits locaux leur ont été expliqués. La rencontre a été précédée, la veille, par les visites des unités agroalimentaires et industrielles. Officiels et participants. Le directeur général de LaNSA, Prof. Komla Sanda a souligné la nécessité pour les opérateurs économiques de se rapprocher de son institution afin qu’elle puisse, non seulement, contrôler la qualité de leur matière première, mais aussi les accompagner dans les choix des procédés de transformation, des techniques et des équipements pour la compétitivité de leurs produits. L’orateur a évoqué les étapes du contrôle de sécurité qui porte sur les contaminants chimiques et la microbiologie. Il a précisé qu’au niveau des contaminants chimiques, le laboratoire recherche les pesticides, les résidus des métaux lourds, des mycotoxines, des colorants interdits et autres additifs interdits utilisés par ignorance. S’agissant de la recherche microbiologique, Prof Sanda a fait noter qu’elle permet de s’assurer du respect des conditions d’hygiène durant la fabrication des produits pour éviter que ceux-ci ne soient chargés en bactéries et en champignon nuisibles pour la santé. Prof. Sanda a affirmé que tous ces aspects sont contrôlés aussi bien pour les produits localement fabriqués que les produits importés dans le pays. Le préfet de Tchaoudjo, assumant les fonctions de gouverneur de région, Tchimbiandja Yendoukoa Douti a invité les opérateurs économiques à collaborer avec le laboratoire non seulement pour la prospérité de leurs affaires mais aussi pour la protection de la santé des consommateurs. Le LaNSA est une institution gouvernementale chargée de garantir une alimentation sans risque à la population. Elle a également pour mission d’accompagner les opérateurs économiques dans la certification de leurs produits agricoles et agro-industriels pour le commerce local et le marché international. ATOP/TAA/MEK/BA

items.title: MTN Ghana extends National Business Pitch to all 16 regions, offers GH¢300,000 grand prize
items.description: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Ghana will have the opportunity to compete for a GH¢300,000 national grand prize under MTN Ghana’s National Business Pitch, which is being extended to all 16 regions. The competition will select 48 businesses, with three SMEs from each region qualifying for the regional contest. Regional winners will receive GH¢30,000 each, while the overall national winner will take home GH¢300,000. Senior Manager for SME Sales, Business Broadband and Partnerships at MTN Ghana, Abubakar Sadiq Mohammed, says the expansion will give more businesses across the country the opportunity to benefit from the initiative. “This time round, we are not going to limit it within a region. We are going to do it in all the 16 regions of Ghana. We have 48 qualified people who will be selected from all the 16 regions,” he said. Mr Mohammed says MTN recognises the important role SMEs play in job creation and economic growth, hence the decision to strengthen its support for the sector. “At MTN, we value the SMEs so much. We believe that these SMEs, when we are able to give them all the necessary support, they grow to become very big companies and create the necessary job opportunities. They also contribute to the GDP of Ghana,” he said. He noted that MTN itself started as a small business and has grown through support and visionary leadership, adding that the company wants to extend similar opportunities to emerging businesses. Mr Mohammed encouraged businesses with valid registration to apply through the designated link on MTN Ghana’s website. He explained that applications would be assessed by independent judges who are not affiliated with MTN, to ensure a fair and transparent selection process. “MTN is not taking part. We have judges who are independent of us. We are going to go through the process with our SMEs and then be able to select the best out of them,” he added. The National Business Pitch forms part of MTN Ghana’s efforts to support entrepreneurship, strengthen small businesses and contribute to private-sector development.

Sudan accuses Ethiopia of launching 162 drone attacks from its territory
items.description: Sudan says 162 drone attacks launched from Ethiopian territory have killed more than 400 civilians and 102 military personnel, amid accusations that Ethiopia is supporting the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The claims have not been independently verified. The accusations were presented at a briefing attended by senior military and intelligence officials and undersecretaries from the foreign affairs and information ministries. Officials identified the locations allegedly targeted as El Damazin, El Mazmum, Sennar, Kosti, Rabak, Belong, El Kurmuk, El Dinder, Wad El Mahi, El Obeid, Abu Oileila, Bara, and Umm Rawaba. They also said dozens of schools, fuel stations, health centres, and hospitals had been destroyed. Sudan identifies alleged drone launch sites The officials said the drones had been launched from bases in Assosa, Bahir Dar, and locations along the Sudanese border, following flight paths alongside South Sudan. They identified several types of aircraft allegedly used, including modified kamikaze drones and long-range models. These included Chinese-made drones and the Turkish-made Bayraktar Akıncı and Bayraktar TB2, they said. Sudanese forces had shot down several drones, including Akıncı and CH-95 models, the officials added. Muawiya Osman Khalid, undersecretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said the government was pursuing a policy of “strategic patience” but would not compromise on defending Sudan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. He called on the international community to take concrete action to stop what he described as aggression threatening civilian lives and regional stability. Sudan says attacks are preventing displaced people from returning Participants at the briefing said the strikes were intended to prevent displaced people from returning to their homes, particularly in Khartoum, and undermine efforts to restore normal life. They also alleged that the attacks risked widening the conflict into a regional confrontation aimed at weakening Sudan. Ethiopia has previously rejected allegations of supporting the RSF, describing them as unfounded. Sudan accuses more than 20 countries of supporting RSF Separately, Defence Minister Hassan Daoud Kabroun said more than 20 countries were involved in Sudan’s war by providing the RSF with logistical support, mercenaries, funding, and drones. In an interview with the Sudan News Agency (SUNA), Kabroun described the conflict as a war aimed at destroying Sudan, plundering its resources, and changing its demographic composition, rather than a civil war or struggle for power. He said the government intended to defeat what he called “the rebellion, militias, and illegal movements”, secure the country, and work towards building a modern democratic state based on transparency. Share article The post Sudan accuses Ethiopia of launching 162 drone attacks from its territory appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Bawumia outlines plans to strengthen NPP policy development and leadership training
items.description: The New Patriotic Party’s 2028 flagbearer, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has outlined plans to strengthen the party’s policy development and leadership training initiatives following a meeting with the Secretary-General of the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS), Dr Mark Speich, in Accra. The discussions, held at the KAS Ghana office on Thursday, October 29, covered Ghana’s political and economic future, the NPP’s internal reorganisation and opportunities to deepen cooperation with the German political foundation. In a Facebook post after the meeting, Dr Bawumia said rebuilding the party remained a key priority, with efforts focused on improving its structures and making it more responsive to the expectations of Ghanaians. He highlighted the Patriotic Institute and the NPP Policy Unit as important components of that agenda, explaining that the initiatives would support leadership development, youth participation and the formulation of practical policies. According to him, the party wants its policy proposals to be informed by evidence, assessed for financial feasibility and designed for effective implementation. Dr Bawumia said the broader objective was to develop an NPP driven by ideas, with stronger structures and a more inclusive approach to political engagement. He also acknowledged KAS’s longstanding partnership with the party and expressed optimism about expanding the relationship in the coming months. The meeting forms part of Dr Bawumia’s engagement with stakeholders as the NPP pursues its reorganisation and prepares for the 2028 general election.

items.title: APSU ’88 gives back to St. Augustine’s College; donates beds, educates teachers on cancer awareness
items.description: The 1988 Year Group of St. Augustine’s College, popularly known as APSU ’88, has returned to its alma mater in Cape Coast for a memorable homecoming to honour the past, strengthen lifelong bonds, and give back to the institution that shaped its members. Held under the theme “Once Classmates, Always Family,” the homecoming brought together the group’s old boys for a series of activities that combined reflection, fellowship, health education, and practical support for the College. The visit underscored the enduring connection between the Year Group and St. Augustine’s College, as members revisited familiar grounds, shared memories of their school days, and interacted warmly with current students and staff. Health education for teachers A major highlight of the homecoming was a health-awareness session organised for teachers of the College. The Year Group presented an educational session on prostate cancer, delivered by Dr John Allotey, a Clinical Pharmacist, an old boy and member of APSU ’88. Dr Allotey took teachers through the fundamentals of prostate cancer, including its causes, risk factors, common symptoms, and the importance of early detection. He also explained the processes of testing and diagnosis, urging men, particularly those above the age of 40, to take regular screening seriously. His presentation further highlighted evidence from Ghana, drawing attention to the growing public-health importance of prostate cancer awareness and the need for timely medical attention. He encouraged teachers to prioritise their health and to share the knowledge gained with family members, colleagues, and their wider communities. The session also featured a presentation on breast cancer awareness, delivered by Florence Hagan, an Oncology Nurse Specialist from the Oncology Department of the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital. Ms Hagan educated the teachers on breast cancer prevention, early warning signs, self-examination, screening, and the importance of seeking prompt medical care. She emphasised that early detection significantly improves treatment outcomes and encouraged women and even men to make regular screening part of their routine healthcare. The two presentations were widely appreciated by the teachers, who described them as timely, practical, and relevant to both personal wellbeing and the health education they can pass on to students and families. Donation of bunk beds As part of its commitment to supporting the College, APSU ’88 presented bunk beds to St. Augustine’s College. The donation was made on behalf of the Year Group by Dr Bill Yeboah Kyeremeh, an IT specialist and member of the group, to enhance the school’s welfare facilities and provide practical support for student care and accommodation needs. The gesture reflects the Year Group’s desire to contribute meaningfully to the comfort and wellbeing of current students. Receiving the beds on behalf of the school, the Assistant Headmistress, Administration, Edith Swanzy-Donkor, expressed profound appreciation to APSU ’88 for the thoughtful donation. She thanked the Year Group for remembering their alma mater and for choosing to support the school in ways that directly benefit students. Madam Swanzy-Donkor noted that the contribution was not only a material gift but also a powerful demonstration of the lasting values of service, unity, and responsibility instilled in old students of the College. Fellowship with students Beyond the formal presentations and donation, members of APSU ’88 shared a memorable lunchtime with the students. The old boys dined with the current students and used the opportunity to interact with them, offer words of encouragement, and share experiences from their time at the College. The interaction created a warm atmosphere of mentorship and camaraderie, allowing students to connect with alumni who once walked the same corridors and sat in the same classrooms. Members of the Year Group encouraged the students to take their studies seriously, uphold the school’s values, and aspire to become responsible leaders in their communities. The following Sunday, the Year Group joined the students again to crown the homecoming celebration. The final gathering provided a fitting conclusion to the visit, reinforcing the spirit of togetherness that defined the entire programme. Commitment to return The homecoming ended with a clear commitment from APSU ’88 to sustain its relationship with the College. The Year Group announced that its next homecoming had been scheduled for October 2028, signaling its intention to continue supporting St. Augustine’s College and maintaining the strong bond among its members. For APSU ’88, the visit was more than a reunion. It was a reaffirmation that, decades after leaving school, the ties formed at St. Augustine’s College remain strong, built on shared memories, mutual support, and a collective responsibility to give back. With its blend of health education, welfare support, student engagement, and fellowship, the APSU ’88 homecoming stands as an inspiring example of how alumni year groups can remain valuable partners in the growth and development of their alma mater.

items.title: Ghana plans local production of active pharmaceutical ingredients to cut drug imports
items.description: Ghana is planning to develop local capacity to manufacture active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), the key components responsible for the therapeutic effects of medicines, as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imported drugs. Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy and Accelerated Export Development Programme, Augustus Goosie Tanoh, says building a domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing industry is critical to achieving healthcare sovereignty and strengthening the country’s ability to meet its healthcare needs. Speaking at the Africa Bio Conference on October 27, Mr Tanoh said about 70 per cent of medicines used in Ghana are imported, while local manufacturers also depend heavily on foreign suppliers for raw materials. He said Ghana must move beyond producing finished medicines to manufacturing the active ingredients used in their production. “Ghana does not produce that active ingredient. We must begin to produce it,” he said. Mr Tanoh disclosed that a proposed 2,000-acre Legon Pharmaceutical Innovation Park, under the 24-Hour Economy Programme and in partnership with Zeme Biohub Limited, is expected to support pharmaceutical manufacturing, research, diagnostics and medical-device production. The proposed facility is also expected to provide opportunities for researchers and start-ups to develop innovations into commercially viable products. He stressed the need for stronger collaboration among researchers, investors and regulators to ensure locally manufactured medicines meet the required safety, quality and efficacy standards. Mr Tanoh further called for priority to be given to medicines for diabetes and other non-communicable diseases, which he said account for a significant proportion of deaths in Ghana. Meanwhile, the President of Sena Institute of Technology and Chief Executive Officer of Zeme Biohub Limited said inadequate infrastructure and funding remain major challenges to the development of Ghana’s biotechnology sector. He said many innovations developed by Ghanaian researchers remain confined to laboratories and fail to reach the market. “All the things we learn or we produce in Ghana, they are in the lab. They are on the shelf; they can’t get into the market,” he said. He said the biotechnology hub is intended to bridge the gap between research and commercial production by providing infrastructure to support innovation, create jobs and help locally developed technologies reach the market. He added that the initiative would help make technology more accessible and enable Ghanaian innovators to commercialise their products locally.

items.title: Sin noticias de José San Emeterio, el hombre que viajaba con Trece, el perro devuelto a su mujer
items.description: Ana Ciprés ayer fue una de las protagonistas tras el accidente de los trenes en Urda. La imagen del Seprona devolviéndole a Trece, su perro bichón maltés, que iba con su marido José San Emeterio, de 58 años (aún desaparecido) en el Ave accidentado en Urda lo han visto millones de personas. Ella estaba ayer en el polideportivo del colegio público de Urda que se improvisó como lugar para acoger a los familiares de las personas que iban en el Iryo y el Ave. Busca sin cesar a su marido junto a sus cuñados Esther y Manuel San Emeterio. “Pepé” decía Ana entre lágrimas. No sabe nada de él desde que ayer recibió la llamada de su cuñado Manuel pasadas las nueve de la mañana. Manuel es un loco de la tecnología y se entera porque le salta un aviso en su reloj inteligente que lleva en su muñeca. Recibió un mensaje automático a su teléfono, configurado como contacto de emergencia. Era su hermano José. Al consultar la ubicación, vio que la señal estaba en medio del campo. “Amplié el mapa y vi que estaba sobre las vías del tren”, explica Manolo. Manuel llama a su hermana Esther. Ponen las noticias y no ven nada raro. Es en la llamada que hacen posteriormente a su mujer Ana, que estaba en Madrid cuando confirman que que José iba en el tren: El vagón ocho del Ave que hacía la ruta Madrid-Sevilla. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Election Night at The Atlantic : Live Special November 3 at 9 P.M.
items.description: The Atlantic will host “Election Night at The Atlantic ,” a live-broadcast special episode of its flagship podcast Radio Atlantic , on Tuesday, November 3 from 9 to 11 p.m. ET, bringing together many of the magazine’s esteemed staff writers to debate the big ideas shaping American politics. The show is an Election Night first for The Atlantic , and will stream from its homepage, on YouTube , and across social media on Instagram , Facebook , and X . Elections are about more than just who wins or loses: They’re a contest of ideas. This will be what animates The Atlantic ’s livestream as the results come in––the ideas that are resonating with Americans, and the future direction for both major parties, institutions, and democracy. Radio Atlantic co-hosts Hanna Rosin and Adam Harris will anchor the live show, and will be joined by staff writers David Frum and Tom Nichols to discuss the future of the Republican Party, Tyler Austin Harper and Mark Leibovich on the state of the Democrats, and Anne Applebaum on what the night’s results mean for American democracy. The livestream is part of The Atlantic ’s ongoing and extensive midterm and politics coverage , which has taken its writers, events, and podcasts around the country to cover key races, issues, candidates, and policy implications. Coverage will publish across the site and on The Atlantic’ s audio network. Also timed to the midterms, Anne Applebaum returns with a fourth season of the Autocracy in America podcast, launching November 10. This season will examine whether we can repair the American institutions President Trump is breaking. Anne will speak with leaders about their plans to work with the administration, to restore international relationships, and to fix the damage done to our economy, as well as what it could look like to retrain and restrain ICE, rescue our cultural institutions, and keep our elections safe. Press Contact : Anna Bross | press@theatlantic.com
